snippet.text: Offline pull request export uses core `PullRequestMembership.storedOwnership` alongside its last membership snapshot. It includes saved members and later conclusively owned rounds from all stores; new unknown candidates stay excluded. Eligible raw stores include the own pull store and stores holding saved or newly owned members. A saved member with explicit foreign ownership causes typed refusal before rendering or writing; refresh and `--accept` retain the audit authority. Before the first snapshot, compatibility export reads only the own pull store and excludes explicitly foreign attributed records. An absent own store reports no snapshot without opening another store or creating its own SQLite file. Added records follow saved members in round-ID order without snapshot numbers. Only actual additions cause an escaped stderr notice and Markdown as-of note. JSON membership and history stay exactly as saved, with no new fields or writes. [The offline ownership amendment](../decisions/2026-10-27-offline-export-stored-ownership.md) records the scope.

message.text: The guideline still says added records follow saved members in round-ID order, but export now sorts those records by mint time.

explanation.what: The guideline still says added records follow saved members in round-ID order, but export now sorts those records by mint time.
explanation.whatToDo: Update this paragraph to describe the legacy-date and mint-time ordering now used for additional records.
explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md requires: "Update documentation in the same change whenever behaviour diverges from what is documented." The new sorting deliberately makes r9 precede r10, unlike round-ID ordering.

properties.failureScenario: With a saved snapshot and additional owned rounds r9 minted at 09:00 and r10 minted at 10:00, export emits r9 then r10. A reader relying on the documented round-ID order expects r10 then r9.
